sourceChecks.claim: AWS ELB introduction confirms distribution across application targets and configurable health/encryption; reverse-proxy flow also matches NGINX proxy configuration. Single-server omission is a workload choice, not a service guarantee.
Azure overview distinguishes transport L4 and HTTP L7/path/TLS offload. Reused connection sticking follows connection-level selection; readable paths require decryption.

NGINX methods define round robin and active-connection minimum; weighted examples bias relative traffic. Unequal work and static weights limit these signals, so conditional measured selection is justified.

AWS health checks specify periodic intervals, consecutive thresholds and all-unhealthy fail-open. The card correctly treats checks as samples and removal as new-selection control rather than rescue of in-flight requests.
Microsoft web-farm app-data/caching guidance requires sharing relevant state and documents session affinity. State only in A is unavailable to B; affinity is routing rather than replication.

AWS deregistration delay stops new requests while awaiting existing connections/work and documents errors on premature termination. L4 reuse caveat follows the earlier routing unit and does not misattribute L7 drain behavior to all products.

AWS idempotency article checked live in this review batch: caller/request token and mutations require atomic durable operation, with equivalent repeated results. This supports shared transaction and rejects isolated check-then-write or memory-only deduplication.

Google overload chapter explicitly says balancing cannot avoid all bottlenecks and requires graceful limits/errors. Headroom, remaining database constraint and reachable alternate frontend are necessary path/capacity conditions, not promises from replica count.
